newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia C.Bank cuts key rate to 24 pct. [corrected 08:25 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Russia C.Bank cuts key rate to 24 pct. [corrected 08:25 GMT]

text.p: Russia's Central Bank is cutting its refinancing rate from June 16 to 24 percent from 36 percent, a Central Bank spokesman said on Friday.

The bank is also cutting the rates it charges on its Lombard lending facility. The bank gave no reason for the cuts, which follow a sharp fall in Treasury bill yields and a steady decline in the inflation rate.
The rate on 3-7 day Lombard loans falls to 18 percent from 24 percent, on 8-14 day loans to 21 from 30 percent and on 15-30 day loans to 24 from 36 percent (corrects previous rate to 36 from 30).
The Central Bank does not operate a formal refinancing facility charged at the refinancing rate, but the refinancing rate is used in many contracts and has an important signal effect.

In practice it is used as little more than a benchmark for interbank lending, but it also serves as an effective cap on Treasury bill yields. Economists have said the Central Bank only cuts the rate when it is sure that yields will stay below the newly set level. Yields have only risen above the rate once -- during the 1996 presidential election campaign.
A 364-day bill issued on Wednesday this week yielded an average 20.03 percent at auction, hitting yield levels targeted by the Central Bank for the end of the year.
